data.name: Vyanraaj
data.gender_notes: Vyanraaj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vyanraaj is a name of Indra, the king of gods in Hindu mythology. He is the god of rain, thunderbolts, and the sky. He is also the king of heaven, and the leader of the gods of the universe. The name Vyanraaj carries the meaning “King of the sky” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vyanraaj usually hope their child will grow to embody king of the sky and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Vyanraaj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King of the sky.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vyanraaj total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Vyanraaj" holds immense importance in Hindu culture as it relates to the revered god, Indra. Indra is an integral part of various Hindu rituals and practices, particularly those associated with agriculture and weather. The name is often invoked during rituals seeking rain, prosperity, and protection from natural calamities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Vyanraaj signifies power, leadership, and protection. Indra, as the king of gods, represents the divine power that governs the natural world. Invoking his name evokes a sense of trust and faith in the divine, offering a reminder that even in the face of natural uncertainties, there is a higher power at work.

vedic_reference.note: The name Vyanraaj is derived from the Sanskrit language. The name can be broken down into two parts: 'Vyana' which means 'circulation of prana or life force' and 'Raj' which means 'king' or 'ruler'. This name is not directly mentioned in any Vedic texts, but it does carry a strong connection to the principles of life and power.

historical_references.reference: The term 'Vyanraaj' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Vy' (all) and 'Anraaj' (king). It was used to describe Emperor Bhoja of Dhar in the 11th century AD who ruled over an extensive kingdom that included Malwa, Gujarat, and parts of Rajasthan. He was a great patron of art, literature, and architecture.

Another reference to 'Vyanraaj' is found in the 'Mahabharata', specifically in the 'Anushasana Parva'. Here, Yudhishthira, the eldest of the Pandava brothers, asks Bhishma, the grand old warrior, about the qualities of a good ruler. Bhishma describes a ruler who is 'Vyanraaj' as one who rules over all, is just, and upholds the moral and ethical values.
historical_references.context: Qualities of a good ruler as described in Mahabharata
